scenes.title: Meet the project
scenes.voiceover: Hi, I'm Elmor. This is a dot net ten web API I built around one idea: keep every feature small, separate, and easy to find. I'll show how it's built, how to run it from scratch, and how AI tooling fits into the workflow.
scenes.caption: Hi, I'm Elmor. This is a .NET 10 web API I built around one idea: keep every feature small, separate, and easy to find. I'll show how it's built, how to run it from scratch, and how AI tooling fits into the workflow.
scenes.actions: Scroll README intro, highlight first paragraph

scenes.title: Technology stack
scenes.voiceover: Here's the stack. Dot net ten and ASP.NET Core. FastEndpoints instead of controllers. FluentValidation for requests. ASP.NET Core Identity with J W T bearer tokens. Entity Framework Core on SQL Server, plus Dapper for one raw query. And Scalar for the API docs.
scenes.caption: Here's the stack. .NET 10 and ASP.NET Core. FastEndpoints instead of controllers. FluentValidation for requests. ASP.NET Core Identity with JWT bearer tokens. Entity Framework Core on SQL Server, plus Dapper for one raw query. And Scalar for the API docs.
scenes.actions: Highlight each PackageReference as it is named

scenes.title: Feature folders
scenes.voiceover: The architecture is vertical slices. Instead of folders for controllers, services, and repositories, each feature gets its own folder. Under Features there's Auth, Product, and Users. Each slice holds its endpoint, request, response, and validator.
scenes.caption: The architecture is vertical slices. Instead of folders for controllers, services, and repositories, each feature gets its own folder. Under Features there's Auth, Product, and Users. Each slice holds its endpoint, request, response, and validator.
scenes.screen: Folder tree of Features/ (from git ls-files)
scenes.actions: Highlight Features/Product/CreateProduct
scenes.result: Four files of one slice highlighted

scenes.title: Anatomy of a slice
scenes.voiceover: Here's the create product slice. In Configure, the endpoint declares everything about itself. The route, the API version, the Admin role, a limit of twenty requests a minute, and its OpenAPI description. HandleAsync maps the request, saves through the DbContext, and returns a two oh one.
scenes.caption: Here's the create product slice. In Configure, the endpoint declares everything about itself. The route, the API version, the Admin role, a limit of 20 requests a minute, and its OpenAPI description. HandleAsync maps the request, saves through the DbContext, and returns a 201.
scenes.actions: Highlight Configure() lines, then HandleAsync

scenes.title: Validation beside the endpoint
scenes.voiceover: Validation sits right next to it. A FluentValidation class says the title is required, and can't pass fifty characters. If a request breaks a rule, the handler never runs.
scenes.caption: Validation sits right next to it. A FluentValidation class says the title is required, and can't pass 50 characters. If a request breaks a rule, the handler never runs.
scenes.actions: Highlight RuleFor Title and Description

scenes.title: Program.cs wiring
scenes.voiceover: Program dot cs wires the shared pieces. Identity, the SQL Server context, J W T validation, CORS policies, and FastEndpoints. Routes get an api prefix and a version prefix, so you get paths like slash api slash version one slash products. Two OpenAPI documents, split by version, feed Scalar. And a custom serializer adds XML next to JSON.
scenes.caption: Program.cs wires the shared pieces. Identity, the SQL Server context, JWT validation, CORS policies, and FastEndpoints. Routes get an api prefix and a version prefix, so you get paths like /api/v1/products. Two OpenAPI documents, split by version, feed Scalar. And a custom serializer adds XML next to JSON.
scenes.actions: Highlight Identity, JWT, UseFastEndpoints, OpenApiDocument, serializers, Scalar

scenes.title: Audit stamps and soft delete
scenes.voiceover: The data layer handles audit and soft delete in one place. On save, the DbContext stamps created and updated dates with the current user's ID. And if you delete a soft-deletable entity, it turns the delete into an update that marks it deleted. Endpoints never do this by hand.
scenes.caption: The data layer handles audit and soft delete in one place. On save, the DbContext stamps created and updated dates with the current user's ID. And if you delete a soft-deletable entity, it turns the delete into an update that marks it deleted. Endpoints never do this by hand.
scenes.actions: Highlight soft delete block, then audit stamps

scenes.title: Dapper for one read
scenes.voiceover: For one read, I used Dapper instead of EF Core. The users list is a paged raw SQL query, joined to roles, and mapped straight into DTOs.
scenes.caption: For one read, I used Dapper instead of EF Core. The users list is a paged raw SQL query, joined to roles, and mapped straight into DTOs.
scenes.actions: Highlight the SQL and the QueryAsync call

scenes.title: Prerequisites
scenes.voiceover: Now, setup from scratch. You need the dot net ten SDK, pinned in global dot json, and a SQL Server. I'm using SQL Server LocalDB. The build passes. It does print a few warnings, including a vulnerable transitive package, and I'll come back to that at the end.

scenes.title: Configuration
scenes.voiceover: Next, configuration. The connection string lives in appsettings dot json. The J W T section is called ApiSettings, with a secret, an issuer, and an audience. I've masked the secret on screen. The development file turns on the database initializer, with migrate and seed both set to true. In production you'd keep migrate off.
scenes.caption: Next, configuration. The connection string lives in appsettings.json. The JWT section is called ApiSettings, with a secret, an issuer, and an audience. I've masked the secret on screen. The development file turns on the database initializer, with Migrate and Seed both set to true. In production you'd keep Migrate off.
scenes.actions: Highlight ConnectionStrings, ApiSettings, DatabaseInitializer

scenes.title: dotnet run on an empty database
scenes.voiceover: For this demo I point the app at a fresh database with an environment variable. Then, dotnet run. On startup, the initializer finds five pending migrations, applies them to the empty database, and seeds the Admin and Customer roles. FastEndpoints registers eleven endpoints, and the app is listening.

scenes.voiceover: Bad input gets rejected. A bad email and a short password return a four hundred, with one message for each broken rule.

scenes.voiceover: Now log in. The response includes a J W T, which I'm blurring on screen. It carries the user's ID and the Admin role, plus an issuer and an audience, and it expires in seven days.

scenes.title: CLAUDE.md
scenes.voiceover: Now, how AI-assisted development fits in. The repo has a CLAUDE dot M D file for Claude Code. It states the stack, the commands, the architecture, and the non-obvious rules. For example, don't hard-delete, and don't set audit fields by hand.
scenes.caption: Now, how AI-assisted development fits in. The repo has a CLAUDE.md file for Claude Code. It states the stack, the commands, the architecture, and the non-obvious rules. For example, don't hard-delete, and don't set audit fields by hand.
scenes.actions: Highlight Overview, Architecture and the data layer rule

scenes.title: Docs as conventions
scenes.voiceover: It also tells the assistant to read the docs folder before generating code. There are four short convention docs: features, API configuration, authentication, and the data layer. So generated code starts from written conventions that a reviewer can check against.
scenes.caption: It also tells the assistant to read the docs folder before generating code. There are four short convention docs: features, API configuration, authentication, and the data layer. So generated code starts from written conventions that a reviewer can check against.
scenes.screen: Code viewer: CLAUDE.md Code Generation Guidelines
scenes.actions: Highlight the four /docs references

scenes.title: The .claude folder
scenes.voiceover: The dot claude folder holds the tooling. A docs-reference-updater agent keeps CLAUDE dot M D's doc list current. A create-docs command scaffolds a new convention doc. A commit command writes Conventional Commit messages, and asks before it commits. And skills cover E F Core migrations, database updates, and moving usings to global usings. Plus skill-creator, for building more.

scenes.voiceover: One more. A Stop hook in settings dot json runs a Python script after each response. It regenerates the project structure tree in the README, so the docs don't drift.
